test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The average weight of P, Q, and R is 45 kg. If the average weight of P and Q is 40 kg, and that of Q and R is 43 kg, what is the weight of R?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight of P, Q, and R = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

Combined weight of P and Q = 40 × 2 = 80 kg

Weight of R = (Total weight of P, Q, R) − (Weight of P and Q)

Weight of R = 135 − 80 = 55 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 55 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight (P + Q + R) = 45 kg

Average weight (P + Q) = 40 kg

Average weight (Q + R) = 43 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of entities

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd470a6cf2b88a40b81248a99ce0d93bca01aafb5ae7480dede4f53ee996d6e1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum (P + Q + R) = 45 × 3 = 135 kg --- (i)

⇒ Sum (P + Q) = 40 × 2 = 80 kg --- (ii)

⇒ Sum (Q + R) = 43 × 2 = 86 kg --- (iii)

⇒ From (i) and (ii):

⇒ (P + Q + R) − (P + Q) = 135 − 80

⇒ R = 55 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 55 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Finding the Overlapping Member

In problems with overlapping sets, the common member (Q) can be found by: (Sum of subset 1 + Sum of subset 2) − Total Sum. Here, Q = (80 + 86) − 135 = 31 kg.

Weighted Average Formula

The average of two groups combined is (n₁ × Avg₁ + n₂ × Avg₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method

If a value is added to a group and the average increases, the new value must be greater than the original average by (Increase in average × New count).
